question: In scikit-learn LogisticRegression, what is the default C and does a smaller C mean stronger or weaker regularization?
answer: In scikit-learn LogisticRegression, the default C value is 1.0 [S1]. A smaller C value means stronger regularization [S1].

citations.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
citations.text:
3. Regularization Strength in scikit-learn
In scikit-learn LogisticRegression the parameter C is the inverse of the regularization strength: a
smaller C means stronger regularization, and the default is C=1.0. For Ridge regression the
parameter alpha works the opposite way: a larger alpha means stronger shrinkage.
L2 regularization (ridge) shrinks all weights toward zero; L1 regularization (lasso) can set some
weights exactly to zero and therefore performs feature selection.

S3.title: Python Debugging Playbook
S3.text:
1. Reading a Traceback
A traceback lists the chain of calls that led to an error. Read it from the bottom: the last line names
the exception type and its message, and the frames above it show the call chain with the most
recent call last. Start with the last frame inside your own code, because frames inside library code
are rarely the cause.
The built-in breakpoint() pauses execution and opens the debugger pdb by default (since Python
3.7). You can also start a script under the debugger with python -m pdb script.py. Inside pdb the
command n runs the next line, s steps into a call, c continues until the next breakpoint, p expr prints
an expression and q quits.
Print debugging still works: print(repr(value)) is more informative than print(value) because repr
shows quotes, escape characters and trailing spaces.

S5.text:
1. Selecting Rows and Columns
In pandas, df.loc selects by label and df.iloc selects by integer position. A label slice such as
df.loc['a':'c'] includes the end label 'c', whereas a position slice such as df.iloc[0:3] excludes position
3.
Boolean masks such as df[df['amount'] > 100] keep the rows where the condition is true.
df.query('amount > 100') expresses the same filter as a string.

What overfitting means in practice A model overfits when its training accuracy is far higher than its validation accuracy. The gap between the two (train accuracy minus validation accuracy) is the simplest warning sign. 2. L2 regularization (weight decay) L2 regularization adds a penalty proportional to the sum of squared weights to the loss, which shrinks weights toward zero without usually making them exactly zero. Advantages: it is smooth, works with gradient-based optimizers, and keeps all features.
